svg.aria-label: Scenario 3, getting the paper ready to submit. You ask: Submit to <venue>. Step 1, across the context boundary, on request before submission, you dispatch sparring-partner in claim-set mode, DECISION_010, which is for after a surprising result, or on request before submission. It receives the proposal as written, lock the claims in RESEARCH_STATE.md as written, for submission, and the evidence paths RESEARCH_STATE.md, EXPERIMENT_LEDGER.md, HYPOTHESES.md and the protocol notes; the premise audit covers every claim and recomputes every number from the ledger rows; it returns a verdict, kill criteria, the strongest alternative and the do-nothing option, the verdict being PROCEED, PROCEED-WITH-CHANGES or RETHINK. It is advice, never a veto, and it never sees the proposer's reasoning; the verdict comes back to you and you decide. Step 2, in your session, /research-master:paper-writer writes or revises and compiles, returning revised sources and a build report after every edit with page count, undefined references and overfull boxes; an equation or derivation goes to /math-reviewer before it ships; it never invents a number, each one coming from results-analyst or a ledger row. Step 3, the script tools/anonymize.py anonymizes: from text files it strips provenance fields, author names, model names, e-mail addresses, session trailers and timestamps, each replaced by a stable label; other files, such as a PDF, are copied unchanged with a warning, and their embedded metadata must be stripped with an external tool before the bundle is handed to a reviewer; the label map is sealed in eval/.sealed/, which reviewers never read. Only the anonymized bundle and the target venue cross the boundary, never the project context. Step 4, dispatch blind-reviewer, a memoryless peer-review panel with exactly one input, the anonymized bundle plus the target venue; with no venue it reviews at a top-journal standard and says so; anything else offered, project memory, decision history, audit notes, what we really meant, is declined. It returns one complete referee report, Editor-in-Chief, three reviewers for methods, domain and clarity, and a Devil's Advocate, with the top three things that must change and the claims that went unverified; it is calibrated to the venue, a preprint server for soundness, clarity, honesty of claims and reproducibility, a journal or top conference for the above plus novelty, positioning versus SOTA, statistical rigor and significance for that community. It never accepts project context and never reads eval/.sealed/ or any project state file. The report comes back through you: you read it instead of re-dispatching for clarifications, then step 5, /research-master:paper-writer revises again, returning revised sources and a build report compared with the last known-good state; committing is repo-maintainer's job; it never re-inflates, a downgraded claim stays downgraded in every later draft. Step 6, on an explicit request from you, dispatch repo-maintainer to commit: the never-push list, enforced by a staging check before every push; it returns the commands run, what was staged, the commit SHA and, every time, confirmation that no protected path was included; it never pushes protected content and never makes a forced push unasked. Footnotes: blind-reviewer hard rule 1, Blindness is the value. No project context, ever; decline it if offered. Sparring-partner hard rule 5, Never a veto. The verdict is advice.
svg.title: Scenario 3 — getting the paper ready to submit
svg.desc: You dispatch sparring-partner in claim-set mode across the context boundary and decide on its advice; paper-writer writes and compiles; tools/anonymize.py builds the blind bundle; blind-reviewer, dispatched with the bundle and the target venue only, returns a referee report through you; paper-writer revises again; repo-maintainer commits.
svg.text: Getting the paper ready to submit
Audit the claim set → write/revise + compile → anonymize → independent critique → revise again → commit — every hand-off goes back through your session.
↑ the verdict is advice; you decide
